screen: MY OFFICE — src/rooms/OfficeRoom.tsx/.css (Desk / Finances / Rivals / Ledger)
roomConcept: /* OBJECT SHOT: looking down ~30° at the owner's desk. */ The office is one desk you never leave — no tabs, no chrome. The camera hangs over scarred oak and a tobacco-leather blotter under a brass lamp clamped upper-left. Everything already sits where it lives: walk-in slips fanned in a wire in-tray on the blotter, a green cloth accounts book lower-right, a string-tied manila folder stenciled THE COMPETITION mid-right, the bound gym ledger half-cropped at the frame's right edge, a dead rotary phone with a paper tag. The player's hands do what a 1975 owner's hands do: pick a thing up (it slides from the bottom third, settles with 1° rotation, desk edges still showing), read it, put it down with Esc. A sliver of the pebbled-glass door — the gym's name painted in reverse — stays top-left: the way back.

objectMap.element: Room shell (.room-screen rounded panel + vignette + breadcrumb header)
objectMap.object: The desk itself, full-bleed: oak top, leather blotter, drawer fronts cropped at bottom edge; a pebbled-glass door sliver top-left with reversed painted lettering names the room
objectMap.behavior: Static set; door sliver is the click target for 'back to the floor' (≥44px), hover = latch jiggle + hinge light-crack; Esc from desk level exits the room (existing overlay-aware handler kept)
objectMap.rationale: Deletes the confessed 'same centered panel' lie; signage replaces breadcrumb text so the room names itself

objectMap.element: Four-tab strip (Desk/Finances/Rivals/Ledger, .office__tabs)
objectMap.object: Four physical objects resting on the desk: wire in-tray, green accounts book, manila intelligence folder, bound ledger — each a one-click pick-up
objectMap.behavior: Hover = lamp glint on the cover + 2px slide toward hand; click = object slides up from bottom third (--ease-paper, ~240ms) and fills frame with blotter visible at edges; Esc puts it down; active state IS the object being in your hands
objectMap.rationale: Same click count as tabs, but wayfinding becomes spatial memory — you reach for the green book, not a label

objectMap.element: Desk tab walk-in queue (.qrow: portrait, name, age, weight class, firstImpression, patience, Review)
objectMap.object: Registration slips: index-card stock (#ece2c8, blue rules), a small paperclipped portrait photo top-left corner, typed name/age/class (Special Elite), pre-printed rule boxes (Libre Franklin 'FORM 3-A'), penciled first-impression quote (Caveat ≥14px, one line), patience as a penciled date ('says he'll wait to Jul 12'); fanned in/under the wire tray, each seeded ±2° by fighter id
objectMap.behavior: Hover = slip slides 3px out of the fan + hot lamp corner; click = slip deals up into WalkInViewer at that index (openWalkIns(ids, i) preserved); after a decision the tray visibly loses that slip within 400ms
objectMap.rationale: A man waiting for an answer IS a slip on your desk; the fan makes the queue readable at rest without a list widget

objectMap.element: Queue count badge in tab label ('Desk (3)') and '.office__count' line
objectMap.object: The visible stack itself plus a typed tray card wired to the in-tray front: '3 WAITING'; exact tally also in the tray's aria-label
objectMap.behavior: Card retypes when count changes; zero = card reads 'NOBODY WAITING' — never a numeric badge
objectMap.rationale: Counts as physical evidence (principle 6); the stack height is pre-attentive

objectMap.element: Impatient state (qrow__patience--low)
objectMap.object: Red rubber stamp 'GETTING RESTLESS' (Anton caps, stamp red #8f3b2e, fixed −2° category angle, seeded ±1° wobble, feTurbulence-eroded) across the slip's corner
objectMap.behavior: Appears when patience ≤3; word + stamp shape carry meaning, never hue alone; normal patience stays penciled date
objectMap.rationale: Urgency as ink slammed onto paper reads faster than a colored label and is period-true

objectMap.element: Empty queue state (.office__empty prose)
objectMap.object: Empty wire tray over bare blotter; the flavor line becomes a pencil note from the trainer left in the tray ('Nobody today. Keep the lights on — word spreads.')
objectMap.behavior: Static; tray aria-label announces empty
objectMap.rationale: Emptiness you can see is more eloquent than centered italic prose

objectMap.element: Future roadmap (FUTURE_DESK 'Book fights' + 'Phase 6' note)
objectMap.object: The dead rotary phone on the desk with a masking-tape tag (Permanent Marker): 'FIGHT BOOKING — line not hooked up yet'; the Phase 6 honesty stays typed small on the tag's back (Libre Franklin)
objectMap.behavior: Disabled = dusty, cord unplugged and visibly coiled; no hover response beyond a dull glint; when Phase 6 lands, the phone plugs in and becomes the booking interaction
objectMap.rationale: A future feature as a not-yet-working object keeps dev honesty diegetic and pre-builds the booking affordance

objectMap.element: Finances: cash on hand + as-of date + low state (.finances__balance)
objectMap.object: The accounts book (green cloth #435243, oxblood spine) opened; current balance is the last handwritten ballpoint line in the balance column, large (numerals 7:1), circled once in grease pencil, dated in the margin
objectMap.behavior: Negative balance = written in red ink per bookkeeping convention + 'OVERDRAWN' penciled beside it; per CD ruling this book is one of the three homes of the bank balance
objectMap.rationale: The number the whole game turns on becomes the line a worried owner circles at midnight

objectMap.element: Monthly summary lines (dues + paying/carrying counts, rent, upkeep, coach salaries or —, net)
objectMap.object: Left page: pre-printed ruled ledger grid (Libre Franklin rules/labels), figures typed in Courier Prime — tabular, aligned, exactly 0° rotation; income in ballpoint blue-black, outgoings in red ink; net under a true double-rule (single rule above, double below, accounting-correct); paying/carrying subline typed small beneath dues; settlement note ('settled the first of each month, {year} dollars') as pencil marginalia
objectMap.behavior: Conditional upkeep line simply absent when zero; '—' for no coaches preserved; #7bbf6a is gone — red/blue ink IS the semantic, redundant with +/− signs
objectMap.rationale: Double-entry red-and-blue is the one place 1975 already had semantic color, so we inherit it instead of inventing it

objectMap.element: The Books history (bookrow: month, dues, out, net, running balance) + empty state
objectMap.object: Right page onward: closed months as Courier rows down the same ruled grid, balance column rightmost and boldest; most recent row in freshest ink (container look, not opacity-on-data); empty state = blank ruled page with penciled 'first month not closed yet'
objectMap.behavior: Scrolls within the page mask (overflow-y inside the book); rows keep all five columns, mobile drops dues/out columns as today
objectMap.rationale: A running balance column read down a bound page is the native 1975 interface for exactly this data

objectMap.element: Credit warning (.finances__warning)
objectMap.object: A bank overdraft notice on white bond, paperclipped askew (+2° seeded) to the open page corner, form-printed (Libre Franklin) with a red 'PAST DUE' stamp; warning prose typed on the notice
objectMap.behavior: Only mounts when money < 0; removed when solvent; never overlaps the figures column
objectMap.rationale: A letter from the bank sitting ON your books is dread you can see before you read it

objectMap.element: Rivals header lede (competitiveness + reputation + magazine pointer)
objectMap.object: Typed appraisal memo stapled inside the folder's front cover: 'NEW YORK IS A CROWDED FIGHT TOWN. WE ARE AN UNKNOWN.' (Special Elite, key facts CAPS+underline, ≥14px); pointer to national rankings as a pencil note: 'nationals — see the magazine on the bench'
objectMap.behavior: Static; reputation word is typed (decision-relevant), flavor framing stays marginalia
objectMap.rationale: Your standing written in your own trainer's dry typewriter voice builds the world's judgment into an object you own

objectMap.element: Rivals scope toggle (local city / regional, .rivals__scope-btn)
objectMap.object: Two die-cut manila tabs on the folder's right edge (clip-path trapezoids, staggered widths, typed labels 'NEW YORK' / 'NORTHEAST'), one dog-eared
objectMap.behavior: Active tab pulled forward casting a hard shadow on the other; click = paper shuffle (--ease-paper, ≤220ms) swapping the sheet stack; real radiogroup semantics, focus ring as brass glint over retained 2px outline
objectMap.rationale: The CD's canonical tab object, used where a tab is genuinely what the fiction contains: a divided dossier

objectMap.element: Gym cards (name, tier chip, manager · style · est. year, fighters of note) + independents card + regional city groups + compact variant
objectMap.object: One typed half-sheet dossier per gym, stapled in a stack inside the folder over a folded city street map (set dressing); gym name typed CAPS underlined; manager/style/founding as the typed second line; tier = rubber stamp per category rule (scouting green-gray, +1.5° fixed, seeded wobble): 'ESTABLISHED' / 'REGIONAL' / 'LOCAL'; independents = a distinct newsprint-stock sheet (#d6d1c2) headed 'UNAFFILIATED MEN' at the back; regional view = the second divider's sheets with typed city headers ruled beneath, compact gyms as carbon copies (carbon look on paper stock only — ink stays ≥4.5:1)
objectMap.behavior: Sheets seeded ±1.5° per gym id; 'No fighters of note.' typed as-is; hover on a sheet = fingertip-smudge highlight; sort orders (tier rank, city alpha) unchanged
objectMap.rationale: A rival isn't a card component — it's intelligence somebody typed up for you, and a folder of dossiers makes scouting feel like work the gym actually did

objectMap.element: Fighter lines in gym cards (name, weight class, record + KO, standing with gold/amber/dim tone)
objectMap.object: Typed columns inside each dossier: name (Special Elite), class and record in Courier Prime — tabular, 0°, no stain may touch them; standing as typed CAPS with redundant shape encoding: RANKED lines underlined twice, CONTENDER once, PRO/PROSPECT plain — tones become ink weight categories, never hue-only
objectMap.behavior: Static data rows; column alignment preserved for down-the-page scanning; mobile column-drop behavior kept
objectMap.rationale: Comparing records is the player's real task here, so this is document-plane law: machine columns at full contrast

objectMap.element: The Ledger (history entries: compact date + text, count, note)
objectMap.object: The bound gym ledger, cloth boards and taped spine, opened to the latest page; dates stamped down the left column (Courier, aligned, 0°), event text in Special Elite with seeded 88–100% word-opacity ribbon variance; entry count typed on the flyleaf card ('214 entries — gyms forget nothing.') and in aria; older entries continue up-page as you scroll
objectMap.behavior: Opens to most recent (reverse-chron preserved); scroll within page mask; entries never re-jitter — seeded by dayCount+index; no timeline, no feed
objectMap.rationale: Principle 8 verbatim: the gym's memory as a book you leaf through makes twenty years of play feel physically accumulated

layout: Controlled asymmetry anchored by light. The lamp's pool upper-left is the eye's entry; the blotter sits off-center left beneath it, so the walk-in slips — the decisions — live in the brightest square of the frame. The accounts book lies lower-right at a seeded −1.5°, its corner overlapping the blotter edge; the COMPETITION folder sits mid-right, one corner under the ledger; the ledger itself is deliberately cropped by the right frame edge (the desk continues beyond the camera). The dead phone and a stained mug fill the upper-right dead zone; the door sliver breaks the top-left corner. Nothing is centered; nothing aligns to a grid — objects align to each other, the way a right-handed man arranges a desk. Picked-up objects settle slightly left-of-center, keeping the tray's slip count visible in the margin. Density is preserved: every datum readable at rest today remains readable at rest or one pick-up away — identical to the current one-tab-click cost.
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: oak desktop (--oak with baked SVG grain tile), tobacco leatherette blotter with brass corner caps (--brass-oxidized), manila folder (--manila), index-card slips (--index-card, blue rules #9fb0bd), green book cloth (--gym-green) with oxblood spine, newsprint sheet, white bank bond, chrome-and-bakelite phone. OFFICE RIG per the vision: one tungsten key upper-left (--key tokens), steep falloff, shadows locked at 3px 5px down-right for every object; rendered as a single pointer-events:none overlay stack — soft-light radial pool plus off-center multiply darkness — above content, so paper and desk are lit in one pass. Components ship flat material colors; paper is lit, never luminous: each picked-up document carries one multiply lamp gradient with a single hot corner. Amber appears only in that pool and in brass glints.
typography: By source, per the type system: SPECIAL ELITE — walk-in slips, dossiers, appraisal memo, ledger event text (the gym's own worn machine). COURIER PRIME — every number: accounts figures, fight records, running balances, dates (clean tabular output, 0° always). LIBRE FRANKLIN 500 — pre-printed rules, form numbers ('FORM 3-A REV. 2/71'), the bank notice. CAVEAT — one-line pencil marginalia: first impressions, patience dates, settlement note (≥14px, never sole carrier of a stat). PERMANENT MARKER — the phone's tape tag. ANTON — stamps only ('GETTING RESTLESS', 'PAST DUE', tier stamps), eroded via the shared filter. Big Shoulders/Oswald/Roboto Slab: deleted.
imperfections: Caused and seeded, two-plane. Environment: forearm-worn blotter edge nearest camera; coffee ring at the blotter's right margin (never under a slip's type); fingerprint smudge on the lamp's brass neck; tape residue where an old tray label was; drawer handle darkened by hands; all scaling with --gym-age. Documents: slips fan at seeded ±2° by fighter id — stable forever; folder dog-eared at one corner; one old accounts line neatly x-struck and rewritten (flavor row, never live data); ledger ink ribbon-varies 88–100% per word; paperclip rust ghost on the bank notice; roughly one sheet in four carries a margin stain. Numeric columns: 0°, untouched, always.
immersionRationale: The current screen's tell is that Desk, Finances, Rivals, and Ledger are the same dark panel wearing different data — the "one reusable component" lie named by the CD. This design makes the four sections four different physical things with different stocks, inks, weights, and resting places, so switching context feels like reaching, not routing. The player learns the desk kinesthetically: money is the green book at your right hand, threats are the tied folder, memory is the heavy ledger you can't quite fit in frame. Decisions land somewhere — a reviewed slip leaves the tray within 400ms, an overdraft arrives as the bank's paper physically on your books. Remove every label and the set still reads: slips waiting under lamplight say 'men want in,' the circled balance says 'we're barely making it,' the dead phone with its tag says 'someday we book fights.' That is the inherited-office feeling stated as the project's final goal.
implementationNotes: Phase 1 is fully CSS/SVG: desk = layered gradients + baked data-URI noise tiles (oak, leather, manila, index, newsprint) as shared tokens; the 30° look is composition, not 3D — flat rectangles, seeded rotate(), one shadow direction; folder tabs = clip-path trapezoids; stamps and torn edges = one-time static feTurbulence defs (never on animating elements); lighting = two blend-mode overlay layers max, per ruling. Keep the existing tab-state architecture (module-scope tab components, stable identity) — 'tab' just becomes which object is held; keep the overlay-aware Esc handler, adding desk-level put-down. Registry slots for real art, delivered neutral/unlit: desk surface, lamp, phone, mug, tray, book covers, map. Risks to flag: slip fan must degrade to a straight column below ~600px width (density guardrail); carbon-copy regional sheets need contrast QA after the lighting layer composites (guardrail 1); the desk-overview adds many DOM layers — cap set dressing at static, no ambient animation, since sessions run hundreds of weeks. ROOM SHOT: standing eye height (~5'8"), just inside the street door, looking across the ring at the back wall. Full-bleed; walls meet viewport edges.
roomConcept: You are standing on the training floor, ten feet inside the street door, keys still in your hand. The ring cuts across the midground — ropes, turnbuckles, a canvas that's been patched twice. The back wall is an elevation of real destinations at honest, unequal sizes: a raised pebbled-glass office door with the gym's name painted on it and light burning inside; a dark corridor to the lockers with a fluorescent gleam on steel; the chalkboard-and-pegboard training station beside the ring apron. On the near right wall, closest to your hands because you use it every minute, hangs the time station: a tear-off date pad and a punch clock. Your hands do three things here: read what the walls tell you, open doors, and tear off days. Nothing on screen is a panel; the five "cards" are demolished.

objectMap.element: Office door (nav → office room, currently 'My Office' card)
objectMap.object: Pebbled-glass wooden door on the back wall, raised two concrete steps, 'OFFICE' painted in sign-painter caps on the glass, gym name arched above it, warm tungsten light burning through the glass from inside
objectMap.behavior: Hover: latch jiggles 2px and the glass glint brightens (light, not fill). Click: door cracks open 8°, 380ms lateral pan + light change into the office. Focus: brass glint on retained 2px ring. Tagline dies; a door needs no marketing copy — aria-label keeps 'Office — walk-ins, fights, finances, rivals'.
objectMap.rationale: The lit glass says 'the business lives in there' without a word; it is the CD's named anchor object and the room's warmest light source.

objectMap.element: Walk-ins-waiting count (red pulsing badge on office card)
objectMap.object: Stack of pink 'WHILE YOU WERE OUT' slips wedged under the office door and into the doorframe, one slip per walk-in, seeded angles; a typed tally card ('3 WAITING') clipped to the door glass
objectMap.behavior: Each advance that brings a walk-in slides a new slip under the door within 400ms (--ease-paper, settle rotation). Click slips: opens the office same as the door. Empty: bare threshold, tape ghost where the tally card clips. Exact count in aria-label and typed on the tally card.
objectMap.rationale: Counts as visible evidence (principle 6): you SEE three men waiting as three pieces of paper someone shoved under a door — the pulse animation becomes an event that physically happened.

objectMap.element: Cash readout (header CASH $2,200 KPI)
objectMap.object: Index card taped beside the office doorframe, typed 'BANK BAL.' with the figure in Courier Prime tabular numerals, yellowed tape at two corners
objectMap.behavior: Static display, always legible (7:1 numerals, card angle 0° on the figure line). Negative balance: figure typed as ($110) accountancy parens plus a red 'OVERDRAWN' rubber stamp across the card's margin — word + shape, never hue alone. Click: shortcut into the office ledger. Updates re-type in place, no tween.
objectMap.rationale: Implements the CD's cash ruling verbatim; a taped card by the office door is exactly where a broke owner would keep the number he checks before every yes.

objectMap.element: Locker Room door (nav → locker room card)
objectMap.object: Open doorless corridor mouth on the back wall right, 'LOCKERS' hand-painted on the header board, cool fluorescent spill and a gleam of steel visible in the dark beyond
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the fluorescent gleam inside sharpens (screen-blend overlay only). Click: 380ms pan into the corridor, warm light crossfades to cool. It is bigger than the office door — a corridor, not a door — size states importance without a grid.
objectMap.rationale: A doorway you can see steel through IS the tagline; warm-to-cool light change makes the locker room a different climate, which is what a locker room is.

objectMap.element: Roster count (parchment badge '8' on locker card)
objectMap.object: Small slate hung beside the corridor mouth, chalk-lettered 'IN CAMP' with a chalk tally-and-numeral ('||||  8'), chalk dust on the ledge
objectMap.behavior: Re-chalks with a 2-frame steps() scratch when the roster changes. Zero fighters: slate wiped, ghost of erased chalk. Count duplicated in aria-label on the corridor button.
objectMap.rationale: A trainer's head-count slate is period-true and readable pre-attentively; tally marks give the count physical history.

objectMap.element: My Gym / training (nav → 'My Gym' card: philosophy, coaches, upgrades)
objectMap.object: The ring itself plus its corner station: a chalkboard on the ring post ('TRAINING' chalked, philosophy word beneath) and a coach pegboard with hanging brass tags — the whole station is one large click target
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the hanging bulb over the ring snaps a touch brighter (light on object). Click: object-shot cut down onto the chalkboard/pegboard (the MyGymRoom view). The CD's three-room ruling is honored: 'My Gym' stops being a fake door — the floor you are standing on IS the gym, and its management view is the ring-corner station you lean into.
objectMap.rationale: Resolves the absurdity of a gym containing a door labeled 'My Gym'; training identity lives at the ring, where it would.

objectMap.element: Coach-applicant count (alert badge on gym card)
objectMap.object: Bill spike on the chalkboard ledge holding applicants' letters — one envelope per applicant, seeded skew, typed tally slip beneath ('2 MEN ASKING')
objectMap.behavior: New applicant: envelope drops onto the spike with paper settle within 400ms of advance. Empty: bare spike. Exact tally typed and in aria.
objectMap.rationale: Men looking for cornerman work mailed letters in 1975; a spike of envelopes is a count you feel.

objectMap.element: The Press (nav → press card)
objectMap.object: Folded newspaper lying on the oak bench in the near foreground, masthead partially visible, reading glasses beside it
objectMap.behavior: Hover: top corner of the front page curls (--ease-paper). Click: object shot — the paper lifts to fill the frame (the press screen), bench edge still visible at frame bottom. Esc puts it down.
objectMap.rationale: Implements the CD demotion ruling: the press was never a room, it was always the paper the owner reads on the bench.

objectMap.element: Calendar (nav → calendar card, plus season display)
objectMap.object: Wall calendar hung crooked (seeded −2°) between office door and time station: 'MAY 1975', month grid with grease-pencil X's through spent days, upcoming fight dates circled in red grease pencil
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the sheet stirs at the bottom edge. Click: object shot into the schedule view. The grid itself already answers 'what's coming' at a squint — circles visible from the room shot. Month name + printed season art carry the season; aria keeps 'Spring, May 1975'.
objectMap.rationale: The calendar becomes what the CD ruled it is — a thing on a wall — and gains at-a-glance schedule info the old card never had.

objectMap.element: Date display + ADVANCE DAY (footer date + button)
objectMap.object: Tear-off day pad on the near right wall, largest print in the room: 'FRIDAY' in Anton, 'MAY 2' huge, '1975' in Libre Franklin form-print, screwed steel backplate, torn stubs of spent days under the staple
objectMap.behavior: Hover: bottom corner of the leaf curls. Click (≥44px, whole pad): leaf tears free, tumbles off with 1.5° rotation (~280ms --ease-paper), next date already printed beneath — never blocks input, reduced-motion snaps. Never disabled. The pad IS the date readout, so advancing time and reading time are one object.
objectMap.rationale: Tearing off a day is the most legible time gesture 1975 owns; the click stays one gesture and the feedback is the data changing physically.

objectMap.element: ADVANCE WEEK (footer button)
objectMap.object: Punch clock mounted directly below the pad: cast-steel case, brass face, card slot showing a typed time card 'WEEK OF MAY 2'; the whole clock is the button
objectMap.behavior: Hover: lamplight catches the brass rim (specular stop brightens). Click: lever slams in 100ms (--ease-stamp, steps(3)), card stamps and drops into the rack, bell tick; hard stop, no ease-out. Never disabled. Aria: 'Advance one week'.
objectMap.rationale: Punching out closes a working week — day is a light paper act, week is a heavy steel act; the material weight teaches the difference in commitment without a '+7'.

objectMap.element: Gym log (collapsible GYM LOG panel, 5 recent lines)
objectMap.object: Corkboard on the left wall near the entrance: latest notes as typewritten slips and pencil scraps pinned overlapping, newest on top fully legible (Special Elite ≥14px), dates penciled in Caveat, older notes peeking beneath
objectMap.behavior: New entry pins on with a damped pin-swing after advance. Click board: object shot leaning in to read all recent lines. Empty: bare cork, old pin holes and sun-faded rectangles. The collapse toggle is deleted — on a wall the board occupies no 'space' to reclaim; nothing is lost, aria lists entries.
objectMap.rationale: A corkboard that visibly accretes paper makes the gym's quiet life ambient instead of a widget you manage.

objectMap.element: HOME / exit (⏻ HOME header button)
objectMap.object: Sliver of the street door at the far left frame edge — daylight through chicken-wire glass — with a red electric EXIT box glowing above it
objectMap.behavior: Hover: the door admits a wider blade of daylight. Click: confirmless, walks out to the home screen with a pan toward the light. The EXIT sign is a fixture, therefore the one legally emissive element on the floor.
objectMap.rationale: The way back stays in frame per the CD shot grammar, and the power-glyph anachronism dies; you leave a building through its door.

objectMap.element: Gym identity (header: name, city/state, 'Local')
objectMap.object: The gym's name sign-painted big and faded across the back wall above the ring (Anton, letterpress bleed), 'NEW YORK, N.Y.' painted smaller beneath; a framed state license by the office door, typed 'CLASS: LOCAL CLUB — N.Y.S.A.C.'
objectMap.behavior: Non-interactive set signage; paint wear seeded from gym id and scaled by --gym-age. Reputation tier re-types on the license when it changes (and in aria). The header bar component is deleted entirely.
objectMap.rationale: Remove every label and the wall still says whose gym this is, where, and how far it has gotten — the brief's final test, passed literally.

objectMap.element: Overlay hosting (ArrivalNotice, Toast, WalkInViewer, RoomRouter, FighterProfile)
objectMap.object: All overlays land as paper on this room's surfaces: notices deal onto the frame's bottom third as slips on the bench; toasts become a slip pinned briefly to the corkboard edge
objectMap.behavior: Deal-in with settle rotation, exit-before-unmount; Esc always puts the paper down; the floor's lighting rig lights them (multiply lamp gradient, one hot corner).
objectMap.rationale: Overlays stop floating in a void; everything that interrupts you arrives as something someone left for you.

layout: Full-bleed elevation, no header, no footer, no centered grid. Horizon at standing eye height; one-point perspective flattened to near-elevation so targets stay honest rectangles. Left edge: street-door sliver + EXIT (the way back). Left wall: corkboard, low, slightly crowded toward the door. Back wall, left-of-center: office door up two steps — the eye's anchor, the only warm lit glass in the room, with cash card and license flanking it. Center: painted gym name high, ring ropes crossing the midground, bench with newspaper in the near foreground breaking the wall plane. Right-of-center: chalkboard/pegboard station at the ring corner; then the taller, darker locker corridor. Near right wall, angled toward camera and largest of all interactive objects: date pad over punch clock — frequency dictates proximity. Calendar hangs crooked in the seam between office and time station. Sizes are deliberately unequal (corridor > office door > chalkboard > calendar > newspaper); baselines drift a few seeded pixels. Nothing is centered; the composition balances mass (dark corridor right) against light (office glass left).
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: painted concrete floor with rubber mats at the ring, gym-green wainscot under plaster-mint upper walls (--gym-green #435243, --plaster-mint #98a58e), oak bench and door casings (--oak), steel time-clock case and corridor gleam (--locker-steel), canvas ring apron, cork, manila, index-card stock, oxidized brass on the clock face. All via baked SVG noise tiles + flat material tokens — no per-component gradients. Light rig (single pointer-events:none overlay stack): three hanging bulbs at irregular spacing, one dead over the far corner; soft-light radial pools on floor and ring; a screen-blend daylight shaft from the street door driven by --daylight/season tokens; warm tungsten bloom inside the office glass; cool fluorescent spill from the locker corridor — the floor's two climates meeting. One shadow direction per the rig (down-right, 3px 5px). Amber appears only in these pools and on brass glints; no control fills amber, ever.
typography: Sign-painter/poster (Anton): painted wall name, door signs OFFICE/LOCKERS, day-pad weekday, EXIT box. Fat-face (Ultra): set-dressing fight bills only. Form print (Libre Franklin 500, 12–14px): calendar grid, time-card ruling, license, pad's '1975'. Typewriter — Special Elite for corkboard notes, tally cards, pink slips; Courier Prime for the bank-balance figure and typed tallies (tabular, 0°). Hand: Caveat penciled dates on the corkboard; Permanent Marker on one taped repair label. Stamp (Anton, eroded shared filter): OVERDRAWN, the punch clock's card stamp. Chalk lettering on slate/chalkboard is drawn SVG strokes, not a font. Every glyph names its maker; no tracked microcaps anywhere.
imperfections: Caused, local, seeded from save/gym id, scaled by --gym-age: hand-smudge darkening around the office doorknob and the punch-clock lever; scuffed threshold arcs at the corridor mouth; rust weeping from the time-clock mounting screws; the dead bulb; tape ghosts and sun-faded rectangles on the cork where old notes hung; chalk dust on the slate ledge; a dated plywood patch in the wainscot ('FIXED 3/71' in marker); calendar hung −2°, corkboard slips ±2° seeded. Iron exceptions: the bank-balance figure, chalk tally numeral, pad date, and calendar grid sit at exactly 0° with zero grain over numerals; stains live in margins only. No two slips or envelopes share a wear variant.
immersionRationale: The current screen is five identical software cards floating over a mural — the CD's 'biggest lie' at its purest. This design deletes the panel as a species: every datum now has a place a 1975 owner would have put it, so the player reads the room the way the owner does — glance at the door for who's waiting, the taped card for money, the slate for head-count, the pad for the date. Frequency maps to proximity (the time station is at your hands; the archive corridor is across the room), so navigation teaches the building's geography instead of a menu's order. Time advancing — the game's heartbeat — becomes two sensorially distinct physical acts, paper and steel, and every advance produces visible consequence within 400ms: a slip slides under the door, a note pins to the cork, an envelope drops on the spike. Things happen TO the room, so the room reads as real. Remove all text and the lit office glass, steel gleam, wedged slips, and torn stubs still tell you everything — the brief's final test.
implementationNotes: Phase 1 is fully buildable in CSS/SVG: the elevation is layered procedural SVG (wall, wainscot, ring ropes as paths, doors as rects with pebbled-glass = feTurbulence baked to a data-URI tile) behind absolutely-positioned HTML buttons whose hit areas exceed the drawn objects (≥44px, especially the calendar and cash card). Lighting = one overlay stack of 2 blend layers max per the CD (soft-light radial pools + screen daylight shaft), tokens --key-*, --shadow-dx/dy. Tear-off pad: two stacked leaves, clip-path tear + transform tumble; punch clock lever: steps(3) transform; chalk = stroked SVG paths with dash jitter. Seeded jitter via a shared hash(entityId) util. Registry slots: back-wall art, ring, door textures — delivered unlit per the amended contract. Risks: (1) room-shot legibility below ~900px — ship a reflow where the elevation becomes a vertical wall-by-wall scroll, time station pinned bottom (never horizontal body scroll); (2) contrast of chalk-on-slate and painted signs must be audited AFTER the lighting composite (4.5:1, numerals 7:1); (3) GymLogBoard collapse and RoomGlyph deletions touch GymScreen.tsx structure — badge() logic survives as slip/envelope/tally counts with aria parity; ROOM_ORDER's five keys still route (gym → ring station, press → bench paper, calendar → wall calendar), so no state or route changes are required, only presentation.

screen: LOCKER ROOM — wall / list / development views (src/rooms/LockerRoom.tsx/.css, src/components/Locker/LockerWall.tsx/.css)
roomConcept: A narrow concrete-block back room under two cool fluorescent tubes: one bank of eight mismatched steel lockers against a plaster-mint wall, a scarred wooden bench bolted to the floor beneath the near row, a brass key rack screwed beside the door frame, a trainer's clipboard hanging on a nail, and the bound Progress Book lying on the bench's far end. ROOM SHOT is the default: the wall of doors IS the wall view, full-bleed, no panel, no header — a sliver of the gym floor's warm light shows through the doorway at the left edge (the way back, Esc). The player's hands do gym-manager work: read doors, lift the clipboard, open the book, hand out keys, stamp fates.

layout: Full-bleed, no centered panel. The locker bank runs from the left third to right of center in two uneven rows — doors are near-uniform but not perfectly: one narrower door (bought secondhand), gaps drift ±4px, the bank sits slightly left of viewport center. The doorway sliver anchors the far left; the brass key rack and hook board cluster on the right wall, breaking symmetry with small dense objects against the large steel mass. The bench runs beneath the near row, trial cards scattered with seeded offsets, weighted toward its right end. The clipboard hangs on its nail between rack and bank at eye height. Stenciled 'LOCKERS' signage, slightly off-level, is the room's only title. Object shots (clipboard, book, orders card) rise from the bottom third and fill ~80% of frame, steel and fluorescent light visible at every edge.
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: --locker-steel doors (#5c635a, lit #757c70) with fresh/worn/old color-mix aging, --plaster-mint block wall above a --gym-green painted wainscot, --concrete floor with a rubber runner, oak bench, brass rack (oxidized, polished only where fingers reach), manila/index-card paper stocks on clipboard and book. Light per the CD rig: two cool fluorescent tubes as screen-blend bands defined once as room tokens, near-shadowless (shadow-dx/dy ≈ 0/2px), one tube on a rare steps() flicker (killed under reduced-motion); warm tungsten spill leaks through the doorway sliver as the sole amber in the room — amber is light falling on steel, never a fill. Components ship flat material colors; the single overlay stack lights doors and paper in one pass.
typography: Special Elite carries the roster sheet and trial cards (worn gym paperwork); Courier Prime carries the Progress Book's compared numerals — tabular, one weight, 0° rotation. Libre Franklin 500 does pre-printed form furniture: column headers, checklist boxes, card numbers ('CARD 7-A REV. 9/74'), tally cards. Anton, eroded by the shared stamp filter, is stamp voice: tier headings, RELEASED, mood/trajectory/feel. Permanent Marker writes tape names on doors and the book spine; Caveat is capped at one-line pencil marginalia (feel blurbs, the dev footnote) at ≥14px. Stencil lettering (Anton, masked) paints 'LOCKERS' and 'TRIALS'. Oswald, Big Shoulders, Roboto Slab: gone.
imperfections: Environment plane, all seeded and caused: smudge darkening around every latch and the clipboard nail; scuffed wainscot at bench height where heels rest; rust streaks under hinge seams and at the key rack screws; one door repainted a slightly wrong green (a dated repair); dents scale with --gym-age. Document plane, capped: roster sheet rotates 1.2° on its clip, trial cards ≤2° each (per fighter id, deterministic); one sheet in four carries a margin coffee ring that never touches type; grain ≤6% over paper; numeric columns and checklist boxes at exactly 0°. The tape name strips fade per tenure — older men's marker is duller ink, a container look, never opacity on live data.
immersionRationale: Every abstraction in this screen becomes something a 1975 trainer demonstrably owned: caps become keys and hooks you can count, tiers become stamped sections of a typed sheet, the dropdown becomes training orders on an index card, cutting a man becomes a red strike and a slammed stamp that leaves a smudge when you change your mind. The three 'views' stop being tabs and become the three things actually in such a room — the wall, the clipboard, the book — so switching views is reaching for an object, which is what management physically was. Consequence motion (a key leaving the rack, a tag swinging onto a hook, tape peeling off a door) means the room visibly remembers every decision within 400ms. Remove all labels and the set still reads: steel = roster, keys = scarcity, bench = men waiting, red stamp = the door.
implementationNotes: Phase 1 is fully CSS/SVG: doors extend the existing lockers.tsx registry (neutral/unlit per the amended contract) with seeded dent/rust layers from baked SVG noise tiles; fluorescent bands are one pointer-events:none overlay stack replacing .worn; stamps/pencil strokes/tape use one-time static feTurbulence defs shared app-wide; the checklist radiogroup and orders-card popover are plain React with roving tabindex. Reuse the room's shadow tokens so paper and steel agree. Risks: (1) the object-shot transition must keep exit-before-unmount cheap — animate transform/opacity only; (2) door glyph slips need aria-labels since visual chrome shrinks; (3) narrow viewports — the bank must wrap without breaking the bench alignment, so bench cards belong to a separate flex row, not absolute positioning; (4) devview keeps min-width + overflow-x inside the book page, never the body. Real art later: door faces, bench wood, key fobs — all behind the registry, lit by the rig.

roomConcept: OBJECT SHOT, office desk. imperfections: All seeded from the fighter's id, deterministic forever: photo tilt ≤2°, memo-slip angle, which divider is dog-eared, stamp wobble ±1°, word-level ribbon variance 88–100%. One folder in four carries a coffee ring — cover margin only, never crossing type. Ghost eraser smudges persist where the standing check used to be; the over-stamped TRIAL under LOCKER is permanent. Numeral columns, ruled scales, and record boxes: zero rotation, zero grain over 6%, no stain contact — jitter the decoration, never the data.
immersionRationale: Every read this screen offers becomes a document a 1975 manager would actually keep, made by a nameable machine or hand — so the player stops parsing UI and starts handling a file. The strongest moves are the ones that give decisions mass: stamping your answer onto the kid's note, the RELEASED stamp slamming diagonally before the folder files out left, TRIAL permanently visible under the LOCKER over-stamp. The fog mechanic becomes physical honesty — a trialist gets a hedged, unnumbered TRIAL sheet with fine print instead of a dimmed widget — and the flight risk is a rival's phone message literally clipped to the corner. Because wear is seeded and permanent, revisiting the same man's folder feels like returning to a real object; because numerals stay typed, level, and lamp-lit, the fantasy never taxes the read.
implementationNotes: Phase-1 is fully CSS/SVG: clip-path trapezoid dividers; baked data-URI noise tiles for manila/card/blotter; stamps and grease-pencil strokes as one-time static SVG defs with feTurbulence erosion (never on animating nodes); seeded jitter via a hash of fighter.id feeding CSS custom properties. Sparkline component re-skins to an SVG polyline with a pre-baked rough-stroke mask — cheap, redraws only on data change. Delete both native selects; the focus clipboard popover needs an Esc-layer guard alongside the existing viewerIds check, and the checklist/radiogroup must keep real radio semantics and the brass-glint focus ring. Verify numeral contrast (7:1) AFTER the multiply lamp layer — tune --index-card if needed. Registry slots for real art: portrait photo print (delivered unlit), blotter/desk texture, drawer face. Risks: request-note overlay pushing folder height on short viewports (let the right flap scroll internally); exit-before-unmount choreography needs a small unmount-delay wrapper; reduced-motion snaps all paper travel.

immersionRationale: The current screen is a data card floating in blurred darkness with three lozenge buttons — the decision is a click. The man is present — a silhouette behind pebbled glass who walks away when you stamp his card — so turning someone down costs a flicker of witnessed consequence, the heartbeat the bible asks for. Capacity stops being a sub-label and becomes countable brass and pad-thickness, so scarcity is felt before it's read. The BANK BAL. line on the desk pad means the money question is answered where the decision happens. And the spike quietly turning dismissed memos into a permanent stack makes even 'Noted' leave a trace in the building's memory.

layout: Full-bleed wall, no centered panel. The painted sign sits high and slightly left, 1° off level. The staff board is the anchor mass — center-left, largest object, under the bare bulb, its five ruled card positions making the staffing math visible at a glance. Right of it, on its own nail 30px higher than feels 'designed', hangs the contractor's estimate clipboard. The HELP WANTED flyer pins in the gap between board and estimate; the wire letter basket is nailed beneath it, letters overhanging. The Personal Attention clipboard hangs lower-left, nearest the door sliver (you grab it on the way out). Baseboard, wastebasket, and a radiator edge ground the bottom. Nothing aligns to a grid — objects align to nails — but every document's internal columns are ruler-straight. Below 720px the wall becomes a vertical scroll: sign, board, flyer/basket, clipboards, in that order.
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: mint-green painted plaster (--plaster-mint) going --concrete at the baseboard, scuffed at hand height; cork in a varnish-cracked oak frame (--oak); --manila and --index-card paper stocks with blue rules; --memo-pink for reply letters; oxidized brass tacks and clipboard clips (--brass-oxidized) with polished glints where thumbs land. Office rig only: tungsten key upper-left (the desk lamp behind you) plus a bare bulb centered over the staff board — rendered as one pointer-events:none overlay stack (soft-light radial pools, multiply darkness at corners), shadows uniformly 3px 5px down-right. Components ship flat; paper is lit by a multiply lamp gradient with one hot corner, never luminous. Amber appears only as light on brass and cork.
typography: Anton: the painted sign, flyer headline 'WANTED', and all stamps (RELEASED, HIRED, PAID, APPROVED — eroded via the shared feTurbulence def). Special Elite: every typed field on employment cards, the flyer body, house-rules card, Personal Attention sheet. Courier Prime: all money — salaries, prices, upkeep, BANK BAL. — tabular, unrotated. Libre Franklin 500: pre-printed form furniture ('FORM E-2 REV. 3/71', 'RELEASE', 'TAKE DOWN', ruled boxes). Caveat ≥14px: one-line pencil marginalia only (personality reads, 'short $438', 'no takers yet'). Nothing else.
imperfections: All seeded, all caused: cards rotate ≤2° per coach.id; your card is two shades darker and dog-eared (it's been up since day one). Fired coaches leave permanent tack holes and sun-faded rectangles on the cork — the board accumulates the save's staffing history, scaling with --gym-age. Estimate sheet: one coffee ring in the margin (never crossing type), carbon smear at the clip. Smudge darkening on the clipboard where it's grabbed; paint drips under the sign; rust at the wire basket's nail. Numeric columns, checklist lines, and money figures: exactly 0° — jitter decoration, never data.
immersionRationale: Every management abstraction becomes something the owner's hands did. Staffing stops being a list with buttons: it's a board with five ruled spots, so the hire cap, the current headcount, and the cost of firing (a hole in the cork that never heals) are all read spatially before a single word. Hiring gains real time and distance — you pin a flyer, letters trickle into a basket, and stamping HIRED physically moves a man's paper onto your wall, which is what employing someone IS. The upgrade pips become PAID stamps with dates, so the estimate sheet doubles as the gym's improvement history. Capacity is blank ruled lines you're not using. And because it's the office's other wall — not a fourth room — the building stays honest: a struggling gym runs its whole business from one small room, and now the player stands in it.
implementationNotes: Phase-1 fully procedural: plaster/cork/paper as baked SVG data-URI noise tokens; card positions via CSS grid with seeded transform offsets (hash of coach.id, same util as other rooms); stamps and torn flyer edge from one-time static feTurbulence defs; checklist is a real radiogroup (replaces the native select — 8 options slightly exceeds the CD's ≤7 inline rule; the flyer is a full sheet so inline stays fine, flag to CD, clipboard-popover is the fallback); letter/card choreography with exit-before-unmount, all ≤400ms, reduced-motion snaps. Tack holes/faded rectangles need fired-coach history persisted (store count or fired ids in save — small schema addition; degrade to seeded generic wear if vetoed). Real-art slots: coach photos (registry entry; 'NO PHOTO' corner until then), painted sign, cork/plaster tiles. Risks: narrow-viewport wall scroll must keep hire/fire targets ≥44px; verify estimate text ≥14px and money 7:1 after the lighting overlay composites.

screen: THE PRESS — newspaper + magazine reading (src/rooms/PressRoom.tsx/.css) and the Monday front-page landing (src/components/ArrivalNotice.tsx front-page + plain-notice modes)
roomConcept: The Press is not a room — per the CD ruling it is the paper itself. OBJECT SHOT: camera looks down ~30° at the scarred plywood bench just off the ring apron, under one hanging bulb. The player has picked up this week's broadsheet, folded to the sporting page; it fills the frame edge-to-edge except for bench wood showing on the right and bottom. The current issue of The American Boxing Monthly lies half-under the paper at the lower-left corner, its cover peeking — click it and it slides on top, already open to the Official Ratings page, the paper's edge now peeking instead. Esc or tapping the bench margin puts everything down and cuts back to the Floor (a sliver of ring light stays visible along the bottom edge). Monday's front page is a different shot: the same paper dealt onto the office desk blotter, still folded.

objectMap.element: Room shell (.room-screen panel, vignette, header chrome, breadcrumb)
objectMap.object: The bench surface itself — full-bleed object shot; no header, no breadcrumb, no panel. The masthead names where you are.
objectMap.behavior: Static resting surface; bench wood visible at asymmetric margins; bottom edge shows a sliver of the Floor's light (the way back). The 'panel' component is deleted, not restyled.
objectMap.rationale: A newspaper resting on wood under a bulb is a place; a rounded panel in a vignette void is the app we were hired to demolish.

objectMap.element: Paper/Magazine tab toggle (press__tabs)
objectMap.object: The other publication physically on the bench: whichever isn't being read peeks from the lower-left corner — magazine cover corner (nameplate + halftone) or the paper's folded ear.

objectMap.element: Paper masthead (paperName + 'Sporting Pages · date' tagline)

objectMap.behavior: Static. Date lives in the folio at full contrast (it is decision-relevant context).
objectMap.rationale: The Roboto-Slab-bold masthead is a 2020 blog header; blackletter-over-double-rule is the single strongest 'this is a newspaper' signal that exists.

objectMap.element: Clippings list (clipping text blocks)
objectMap.object: Real sports-page stories: 2–3 justified, hyphenated Noticia Text columns separated by hairline column rules; each story gets an Anton headline deck (1–3 sizes by story weight) or runs under a standing column head; stories separated by cut-off rules, not card borders.
objectMap.behavior: Static reading. No hover states — paper does not react to eyes. Break-inside avoid preserved; long weeks simply make a longer page that scrolls as one sheet.
objectMap.rationale: Headline hierarchy is how a reader triages a page in two seconds — the current uniform gray blocks lose the information scent a real sports page gives for free.

objectMap.element: Clipping date (clipping__date, currently tracked red microcaps)
objectMap.object: Agate dateline opening the story's first line: 'NEW YORK, Apr 27 —' in Libre Franklin 12px, news black.
objectMap.behavior: Inline, unrotated, full contrast. The tracked-red-microcaps overline pattern is deleted per the noList.
objectMap.rationale: Newspapers never printed floating date labels; the dateline is the period-true carrier of exactly the same datum.

objectMap.element: Byline (clipping__byline '— Paul Turner')
objectMap.object: 'By PAUL TURNER' agate byline under the headline deck; the recurring 'AROUND THE GYMS' items instead run under a standing boxed column head with the writer's name beneath it, same column position every issue.
objectMap.behavior: Static. Writer names are persistent world data, so the standing column belongs to the same man forever.
objectMap.rationale: A named column the player learns to trust ('Grossman's long-lunch item is never nothing') turns bylines from decoration into a relationship.

objectMap.element: Empty paper state (paper__empty)
objectMap.object: The page still prints: a one-column brief under the head 'QUIET WEEK ON THE LOCAL BEAT' (the existing copy as body text), padded with a period house ad ('FRIDAY BOUTS — BROTHERHOOD ARENA — GEN. ADM. $3') as filler.
objectMap.behavior: Static; the house ad is set dressing (aria-hidden), the brief carries the real message.
objectMap.rationale: A newspaper with a blank page breaks the fiction harder than any panel; slow news filled with ads IS 1975.

objectMap.element: Magazine masthead (MAGAZINE_NAME, tagline, 'Official Ratings · year')
objectMap.object: A Ring-style monthly open to its ratings page: whiter coated stock than the newsprint, nameplate in Ultra fat-face, tagline in italic-free Noticia beneath, 'WORLD OFFICIAL RATINGS — 1976' as a ruled department head; a typed subscriber mailing label ('SUBSCRIBER — HELL'S KITCHEN BOXING, NEW YORK') sits crooked on the visible cover corner when tucked away.
objectMap.behavior: Arrives already open (no cover-flip click tax). Dark-glossy-panel styling is deleted; ink is news black on paper.
objectMap.rationale: The mailing label says the gym has subscribed for years — world-building in one seeded sticker — and paper-white ratings finally read at 12:1 instead of amber-on-leather.

objectMap.element: Division sections (magazine__division / divname)
objectMap.object: Ratings boxes exactly like The Ring's: 'HEAVYWEIGHT' in Anton caps inside a ruled box with a double rule above, divisions stacked heavyweight-first down the page.
objectMap.behavior: Static structure; empty divisions omitted as now.
objectMap.rationale: The ruled ratings box is the most recognizable artifact in boxing print history — instant authority, zero explanation.

objectMap.element: Rank rows (rankrow: rank, name, camp, record)
objectMap.object: A leader-dot ratings table: '1. KENNETH GALLAGHER ..... 21-6-0 (12 KO)' — rank + name in Libre Franklin 500 caps, camp in 12px roman beneath or beside the name, records in Courier Prime tabular figures, right-aligned, 0° rotation.
objectMap.behavior: No hover, no zebra striping. Records column is the sacred data plane: aligned, unrotated, no grain over numerals.
objectMap.rationale: Leader dots carry the eye from name to record the way flexbox gaps never will, and Courier record columns scan vertically for comparison — the actual job of a ratings page.

objectMap.element: Player's own fighters appearing in the ratings
objectMap.object: A grease-pencil circle (seeded SVG ellipse, graphite #4a463f at ~85%) around the row of any fighter whose camp is the player's gym, drawn in the margin gutter so it never crosses the numerals.
objectMap.behavior: Deterministic per fighter id; appears only when the player's man is ranked. Purely additive flavor — the row underneath stays full contrast.
objectMap.rationale: The owner circling his own boy in the national ratings is the proudest mark a struggling gym ever makes; it also makes the player's stake in the page pre-attentively findable.

objectMap.element: Front page mode (ArrivalNotice newIssue: masthead, dateLabel, headlines ≤5, quiet-week line)
objectMap.object: Monday's paper landing folded on the office desk blotter: above-the-fold only, a horizontal fold crease shading the lower edge, dealt in with 320ms --ease-paper and ~1° settle; blotter leather and desk-lamp pool visible at the frame edges; headlines get one lead Anton deck + smaller decks; empty week prints the 'quiet week' one-column brief.
objectMap.behavior: role=alert kept; reduced-motion snaps. The centered modal, scrim, and rounded corners are deleted.
objectMap.rationale: News arriving as a thing that lands on your desk — not a dialog that interrupts you — is the difference between living in 1975 and being notified about it.

objectMap.element: 'At your gym' strip (arrivals, expired, departed, poached lines)
objectMap.object: A rule-boxed single-column brief on the front page under the printed head 'AT YOUR GYM' (boxed briefs are real newspaper anatomy); each event is one typeset line at full contrast; the actionable arrivals line gets a grease-pencil circle in its margin.
objectMap.behavior: Renders only when events exist (as now); departures and poachings are set as plain news lines — bad news in print stings correctly.
objectMap.rationale: Your gym appearing IN the paper, boxed like any local item, sells that the world watches you; the pencil circle is the owner's own hand flagging what needs doing.

objectMap.element: Front-page actions (Review at the door / Read the full paper / To the floor)
objectMap.object: Three physical affordances: a memo-pink 'WHILE YOU WERE OUT' slip paper-clipped to the paper's top corner reading '2 MEN WAITING AT THE DOOR' (click = viewArrivalsNow, shown only when hasArrivals, exact count typed on it); the folded lower edge of the paper labeled in agate 'Cont. on Sporting Pages' (click anywhere on the fold = open The Press); the blotter margin around the paper (click/Esc = dismiss to floor).
objectMap.behavior: All targets ≥44px with full aria-labels ('Review 2 fighters at the door'); slip hover lifts 1px under its clip; fold hover brightens under the lamp; each is one click, matching current cost.
objectMap.rationale: Unfolding a paper to keep reading and answering the slip clipped to it are motor memories from a real desk — three buttons in a row are motor memories from Figma.

objectMap.element: Plain mid-week notice (non-newIssue mode: eyebrow, lines, View Now / View Later / Noted)
objectMap.object: A single memo-pink 'WHILE YOU WERE OUT' pad slip on the blotter, typed lines (Special Elite) for each event; 'View Now' is the paper-clip slip pull (click the slip body), 'View Later / Noted' is sliding it into the wire in-tray at the frame edge (click the tray or Esc).
objectMap.behavior: Slip deals in with settle rotation (seeded ≤2°); filing to the tray animates 260ms then dismisses; the tray visibly holds the slip afterward, count in its aria-label.
objectMap.rationale: Mid-week events are gym business, not news — the pink slip keeps the notification system one consistent object everywhere in the game, per the CD's objectSystem.

layout: The broadsheet dominates: full-bleed sheet rotated a seeded 0.7°, but its interior grid — masthead, double rule, three columns with hairline rules — is rigidly straight, so the crookedness lives in the object, never the type. Asymmetry is physical, not compositional: more bench shows on the right (≈70px) than the left (≈20px), the magazine corner breaks the lower-left edge, the fold ear breaks the top-right. The eye lands on the nameplate, drops through the lead Anton deck (top-left column, largest), then triages by deck size — real newspaper wayfinding replacing whitespace hierarchy. The Magazine swaps in at the same footprint but whiter, tighter, single-column ratings boxes stacked heavyweight-first. The Monday front page sits smaller and folded on the blotter, upper-left of frame, pink slip clipped at its corner, lamp pool anchoring the top-left.
materialsAndLight: Surfaces: --newsprint (#d6d1c2) with the shared baked paper-noise tile and a faint halftone dot tile in image areas; magazine on brighter coated stock (index-card white, subtle screen-blend sheen band that shifts 4px on pickup); bench in stained plywood/oak tokens with visible grain gradient; front page rests on the office blotter leather. Light: the Floor rig — one hanging tungsten bulb, a soft-light radial pool upper-center of the sheet, multiply darkness pushing the bench corners down; the paper is lit, never luminous. Front page uses the Office rig: lamp upper-left, shadows 3px/5px down-right, one hot corner on the page. Amber appears only in these overlays; every ink on paper is news black or ribbon gray.
typography: By source: UnifrakturMaguntia for one masthead word only; Anton for headline decks, standing column heads, and division heads; Ultra for the magazine's fat-face nameplate; Noticia Text justified/hyphenated for all story body; Libre Franklin 500 for agate — datelines, bylines, folios, ratings names; Courier Prime tabular for records and KO counts; Caveat only as the grease-pencil circles' implied hand (marks, not text); Special Elite on the pink slips. Oswald's tracked microcaps (tagline, dates, tabs) are deleted everywhere on this screen.
imperfections: Seeded per issue (hash of dayCount): fold crease shading, one dog-eared corner, ±0.7° sheet rotation, 1px ink misregistration on the nameplate only, ragged left deckle on the sheet edge (SVG clip-path, generated once). Bench: cup ring, tape residue, one cigarette scorch at the margin — environment plane, unlimited. Magazine: scuffed spine, crooked subscriber label (seeded −1.5°), thumbed corner. Front page: coffee ring in the blotter margin, never touching type. Grain ≤6% over text; ratings columns, records, and the yourGym lines stay at 0° and full contrast — jitter the decoration, never the data.
immersionRationale: The current screens tell you news exists; this design makes you read the news the way the owner does — pick up the paper off the bench, thumb to the sporting page, find your own gym boxed in column three. Every trust signal is diegetic: the standing column teaches you which writer's rumors matter; the subscriber label proves the gym has taken the Monthly for years; the grease-pencil circle around your ranked fighter is the owner's pride made visible. Monday stops being a modal and becomes the morning ritual of 1975 — the paper lands on the blotter, a pink slip is clipped to it, and you answer the slip or unfold the page with the same gestures a real desk demanded. Remove every label and the scene still says: small gym, one bulb, the whole sport arriving as ink.
implementationNotes: Phase-1 is fully CSS/SVG: column-count + column-rule already exist; add hyphens:auto (needs lang='en' on the sheet), leader dots via dotted border-bottom flex fillers, halftone/newsprint as data-URI tiles, fold crease and lamp pools as gradient overlays (shading only — never transform text halves), deckle edge and grease-pencil ellipse as one-time static SVG defs, seeded by entity id. Data changes needed: press.ts clippings gain an optional headline field (fallback: derive standing-column head from templateId prefix like 'AROUND THE GYMS'); rankedElite rows need a 'isPlayerCamp' check (campOf vs save gym name) for the pencil circle. Fonts: subset UnifrakturMaguntia to the masthead word's glyphs (~4KB) and Ultra to the nameplate. Needs-real-art slots: magazine cover halftone photo (phase-1: SVG duotone silhouette), house-ad art. Risks: justified narrow columns can river — set min column width 240px; keep the publication-swap animation exit-before-unmount so mid-read remount bug (noted in the TSX comment) stays fixed via stable component identity.

screen: HOME / NEW GAME / SETTINGS / CALENDAR placeholder (src/screens/HomeScreen.tsx/.css, src/screens/newgame/*, src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx, src/rooms/RoomPlaceholder.tsx)
roomConcept: The first frame of the film is the street. Night, 1975. ROOM SHOT: standing on the sidewalk facing the gym's storefront — brick, a pebbled-glass door, and a big painted window with THE SWEET SCIENCE in chipped gold leaf. A sodium streetlamp pools light from upper-left; a tungsten lamp burns somewhere inside, glowing through the glass. Your hands hold a key ring. Continue is the key already in the deadbolt; New Game is the FOR LEASE card taped inside the window; Settings is the steel service panel beside the door. New Game cuts to an OBJECT SHOT: the landlord's desk, a three-page carbon lease packet under a paperclip, a pen, a road map, a rack of city cards. You are not choosing menu options — you are deciding whether to unlock a door or sign a lease.

layout: Home: full-bleed storefront, no centering. The door sits right of center at true architectural scale; the painted window dominates the left two-thirds and holds the title high, the FOR LEASE card low-left (natural eye path: sign, then lease card, then door). Service panel hangs at hip height on the far right wall; permit tag in the window's bottom corner; sidewalk and curb ground the bottom edge. The streetlamp's pool anchors the eye on the door hardware — the actual primary action. New Game: object shot at ~30°, lease packet filling the frame but offset left, road map and card rack breaking the right edge, blotter visible all around. City step goes asymmetric two-column: typed index rack left (narrow), map with pulled card right (wide). Nothing is symmetric; everything rests on the desk.
materialsAndLight: Street: sooted brick, pebbled wire-glass, gold leaf, painted steel panel, concrete sidewalk. Two named sources: sodium streetlamp upper-left (the room's key; shadows fall 3px 5px down-right) and warm tungsten interior glow bleeding through the door glass — the only amber on screen, applied as screen/soft-light overlays above content per the rig contract. Desk scene: office rig verbatim — tungsten lamp upper-left, steep falloff, one hot corner on the paper (multiply gradient). Paper stocks: --manila lease packet, --index-card city cards and license, --pulp map, --memo-pink landlord note. Panel interior lit by the streetlamp spilling in, near-shadowless steel. All fills flat material color; light lives only in the overlay stack.
typography: Window sign: Ultra fat-face arc for THE SWEET SCIENCE, Anton for the painted subtitle and the SERVICE stencil. Lease/license pre-print: Libre Franklin 500, 12–14px, with form numbers ('FORM CL-7 REV. 9/71'). Player-typed fills and city index: Special Elite; city card body and comparative data: Courier Prime, tabular, 0°. Stamps (SELECTED, FILED, RETAKE): Anton caps through the shared erosion filter, fixed category angles. Pencil marginalia ('Press Enter when it feels right', checklist checks, signature): Caveat ≥14px, one-read flavor only. Masking-tape labels in the panel: Permanent Marker. Big Shoulders/Oswald/Roboto Slab deleted from all four screens.
imperfections: Gold leaf chipped along letter bottoms; one letter of SCIENCE repainted brighter than its neighbors (an old repair, dated in tiny painter's script). Ghost rectangles of tape residue from posters that used to hang in the window. Rust streaks under the panel's screwheads; brass worn bright around the keyhole where hands go. The lease packet: coffee ring in the left margin of page 1 only, never crossing type; page 3's carbon pre-print is fainter (container flavor — typed fills stay full contrast). City cards rotate seeded ≤2°; the index column rotates 0°. FOR LEASE card yellowed at the tape. All seeded per install id, deterministic, never re-rolled.
immersionRationale: The current home screen is a logo over a vignette — it tells you the genre; the storefront shows you the premise. Standing outside at night with a key encodes the entire fantasy (this building is yours to keep alive) before one word is read, and it passes the remove-all-labels test: door, lease sign, service panel each self-describe. Making New Game a lease you sign converts a wizard into the founding memory of the save — the stepper, inputs, and city picker all gain stakes because they're marks on a legal document. The opening scene's payoff (your name freshly painted where FOR LEASE hung) closes the loop with consequence motion, so the player's first Advance-Day happens in a building they watched themselves acquire. Continue-as-key makes every return session a homecoming.
implementationNotes: Phase 1 is fully CSS/SVG: storefront as one SVG scene (brick via baked noise tile + gradients, pebbled glass via feTurbulence-baked tile with the interior glow behind it, gold leaf as filled text with layered hard shadows) with three absolutely-positioned DOM hit regions (door, lease card, panel) ≥44px, cursor + hover-light affordance, brass focus-visible ring. It drops into the existing background asset registry delivered neutral/unlit per the rig ruling — real painted-storefront art replaces it later without relayout. Lease/license/cards are DOM+CSS (real inputs, radiogroups, listbox — keep current roles and Enter/Esc handling verbatim). One-time signature draw-on uses stroke-dashoffset; photo flash and door-crack respect prefers-reduced-motion. Risks: scene-object discoverability at first launch (mitigate with signage text and the streetlamp pool aimed at the door); small-viewport storefront needs a clamp()-based scale with the window sign allowed to crop before controls do; 'The temporal hub' and 'My Office' copy in src/game/rooms.ts violates the noList and must be rewritten to sign-painter language when RoomPlaceholder is rebuilt.
